items.text: Confirm address + gate/alarm codes + key/lockbox (log on the customer record, not loose paper)
Know the plan (what this owner pays for) + any add-ons (package pickup, contractor meet-in)
Phone charged — every visit ends in a photo/text report

sections.name: On-site checklist — walk it the same way every time

items.text: Walk the full perimeter — roof/eaves, siding, foundation, windows, doors
Storm/wind damage, fallen limbs, debris
Signs of pests/animals, wasp nests, standing water
Doors & windows secure; no break-in signs
Decks/rails, exterior lights, HVAC condenser unit
Each room: leaks/water stains (ceilings, under sinks, water heater), smell for mold/musty
Run water / flush toilets; check no slow drains
HVAC running, thermostat at the set point (humidity control matters off-season)
Breaker panel normal, no tripped breakers; fridge/freezer if owner asked
Pests (droppings, ants, roaches), any alarms/leak detectors
Re-lock, reset alarm, return key to lockbox
Send the photo + text report (2–6 photos + a one-line "all good" or the issue found)
Found a problem? Note it, photograph it, and flag to Ray — do not authorize repairs (owner decision)
Mark visit complete in the app

guards: Anything that looks like real damage or a safety issue → document + escalate to Ray same day; don't try to fix it.
Keep codes/keys controlled — never leave them in the open or text them in plain view.
checklists.title: Home-Watch
checklists.pricing_guardrail: monthly $50/visit · bi-weekly $45 · weekly $40 · one-off $75 · storm check $95. Recurring = the goal. ~30–45 min/visit incl. drive. Near-zero materials.

sections.name: Know the difference (lead with the right one)

items.text: Soft wash = low pressure (~100 PSI) + SH/surfactant mix. Roofs, siding, stucco, screens, painted surfaces. Kills algae/mildew, lasts longer.
Pressure wash = high pressure. Concrete only — driveways, sidewalks, dumpster pads, decks (carefully). Never pressure-wash shingles (strips the granules) — roofs are soft-wash, always.
Walk the property; note surfaces + size (confirm the quote tier)
Plant protection: pre-wet + tarp/cover landscaping near the work; have the plant-rinse ready
Water source (customer spigot) + buffer tank if flow is weak
Mix the right ratio: siding ~2.5% SH; concrete/masonry steps up to ~4%; add surfactant ~1 oz/gal
2-story/roof: ladder footed on solid ground, stabilizer on, second crew member spotting the ladder — never solo on a ladder
Pre-rinse surface + surrounding plants
Apply solution low-pressure, work bottom-up, let it dwell (don't let it dry on the surface)
Agitate/spot-treat heavy stains
Rinse top-down; re-rinse all plants/landscaping thoroughly
Basic cleanup — coil hoses, no chemical containers left out

guards: PPE on for SH: chem gloves, eye protection, and on roofs face shield + non-slip footwear. Mind overspray onto cars/neighbors.
3-story, steep, or anything past safe ladder reach → refer, don't improvise.
Recurring close: every one-off wash → offer the annual plan before you leave; log it for Ray.
checklists.title: Soft / Pressure Washing
checklists.pricing_guardrail: house soft-wash 1-story ≤1,500 sqft $299 · ≤2,500 $399 · 2-story 2,500–3,500 $549 · roof soft-wash from $399 · driveway $99/$149/$199 by size. Recurring 20% off. House wash 3–5 hrs; driveway 1–2 hrs.

items.text: Mow at the right height (don't scalp coastal lawns)
String-trim fence lines, beds, obstacles
Edge hard surfaces (walks, driveway)
Blow clippings off all hardscape — leave it cleaner than found
Quick walk for trash/limbs; bag and haul what's there
Photo the finished yard for the route log
Hedge/shrub trimming, leaf/debris cleanup, mulch refresh (mulch billed as a materials line, cost + markup).

Limb/branch + small-tree work: in scope only if reachable from the ground or the 30-ft ladder — no climbing, no large trees. Use the AP chainsaw/pole saw. Anything bigger or up high → refer to a tree service (note it for Ray).

Clean vegetative debris (brush, leaves, grass, pine straw) dumps FREE at the Dare County C&D landfill / Public Works recycling. Keep green waste clean and separate — the second you mix in bagged trash or lumber you lose the free rate and pay $73.16/ton.
Lot size + slope + obstacle density (sizing the visit)
Travel/zone: remote north (Corolla/Carova) → higher minimum + travel line; bundle remote stops on one route day
Recurring vs one-off — push the recurring plan

guards: Ear + eye protection on all powered equipment; label gas cans (right mix — wrong fuel kills 2-strokes; AP tools are battery, but check any gas backups).
Over a crew-day or needs a third body (big overgrown lot) → price to sub / flag Ray, don't absorb it.
checklists.title: Mowing / Yard Routes
checklists.pricing_guardrail: mow + trim + edge from $45/visit (recurring 20% off) · hedge trimming from $89 · debris cleanup & haul from $99 · large/oversized lot from $69/visit. Flat per visit, never hourly.

items.text: Bed-bug question (scripted, not rude): "Standard question for anything with fabric — any history of bed bugs?" Carry zip mattress/sofa bags + sealed contractor bags + gloves. Right to decline or surcharge infested items — one infestation can contaminate the truck and every job after it. Non-negotiable.

Furniture sizing — don't undersize. A "love seat" is a 2–3 seater; sofas/sectionals/recliners eat space. Confirm counts and real sizes so the load fits (the "love seat = small chair" miss cost us truck space).
Access assessment: stairs, floors, long carry, driveway blocked by cars → access-difficulty bump in the price.
Travel/zone: remote north → higher minimum + travel line; bundle remote stops.
One scheduled trip. Set up front: this clearing is one trip; extra trips are billed. (Repeat callbacks are the margin killer.)
Movers finish FIRST → then junk → then cleaners. Never work around active movers. Confirm the movers are DONE before we roll — no repeated callbacks while they're still going.

"Authorized for disposal" sign-off: get explicit confirmation (text/app) that everything remaining is cleared to toss. Removes keep-vs-toss guessing and protects us from "you threw away my X." If there's no clear call on an item, set it aside, don't toss it.
Walk the full scope with the customer; confirm what's going
Protect floors/walls on the carry-out (blankets, straps)
Load smart; set aside resaleable items (log them — resale is real money, but never take anything not authorized)
Separate clean vegetative/recyclable from C&D where it saves dump fees
Sweep/broom the cleared space — leave it better than found
Before/after photos for the review ask

Price the dump fee into the job every time: estimate the load, add tonnage (~$73.16/ton mixed C&D, first 500 lb free; clean veg = free), then labor + margin on top. This is the line new haulers eat by accident.
Confirm the customer's happy with the cleared space (photo walk-through)
Invoice through the app + drop the review link
Note any resale items recovered

guards: Hazardous (paint, chemicals, propane, fuel) → don't haul; flag for separate handling.
Over the two-person ceiling (huge hoarder load, needs a third body / multiple days) → price to sub or stage over scheduled billed trips — flag to Ray, don't absorb it.
Disorganized customer pushing extra trips/scope → hold the line politely; one trip quoted, more is billed.
checklists.title: Junk Removal / Clear-Outs
checklists.pricing_guardrail: $350–850 typical · whole-house clear-out $1,200–2,500 · price on site by volume (truck/trailer-bed fraction) + dump fees + access. Flat per job, never hourly.

items.text: Parking-lot & roadside litter, dumpster-area cleanup, storefront/sidewalk debris, post-event cleanup, light grounds policing.
Recurring is the play — sell the scheduled plan and document each visit with photos.
Walk the area; note hazards (broken glass, sharps, biohazard → gloves/grabber, don't hand-pick)
High-vis vest + cones if near traffic/lot drive lanes
Litter/debris pick + bag (contractor bags)
Dumpster area: pick stray debris, sweep pad, push-broom corners
Storefront: sidewalk sweep, entry debris, gum/stain spot-treat if quoted
Haul bagged waste; confirm where it goes (customer dumpster vs. our haul + dump fee)
Before/after photos → send with the visit log (this is what makes recurring sticky)
Lot/area size + how trashed it is (frequency drives the recurring price)
Disposal: customer's dumpster (free) vs. we haul (add dump fee)
Travel/zone bump for remote sites; bundle into a route

guards: Biohazard/sharps/hazmat beyond basic litter → don't handle; flag to Ray.
One-off that balloons into a haul-off → re-quote as a junk job (SOP 04), don't eat it.
checklists.title: Cleanup (Residential + Light-Commercial)
checklists.pricing_guardrail: priced by lot size / scope · recurring plans 20% off (daily/weekly/monthly). Flat per visit.

items.text: IN: ground-based brush, overgrowth, saplings, limbs/branches and small trees reachable from the ground or the 30-ft ladder.
OUT → refer: climbing, large trees / big trunks, anything above ~30 ft or needing a controlled drop. We are not a tree-removal service.
Walk the area; identify property lines, utilities, septic, irrigation, anything to protect
Spot hazards: power lines (stay well clear), ground hornets/snakes, poison ivy, soft/wet ground
Confirm what stays vs. goes with the customer (mark keepers)
Gear: AP chainsaw/pole saw, loppers, machete, rakes, tarps; rent brush mower/chipper if the volume calls for it (pass-through line)
PPE: chainsaw chaps whenever the saw runs, eye + ear protection, gloves, boots; hard hat if overhead limbs
Cut low-to-high, drag to a staging pile, feed chipper or load for haul
Keep vegetative debris clean/separate → dumps FREE (don't mix with trash/C&D)
Rake and clear the worked area; haul off
Before/after photos
Density + area (how thick, how big)
Rental needed? (brush mower / chipper / stump grinder — stump grinder still rented ~$85–160/day)
Disposal volume (free if clean veg; chipping cuts haul trips)
Access + travel/zone bump

guards: Anything past the reach cap, near power lines, or needing a climber → stop and refer. No exceptions.
Bigger than a crew-day or needs a third body → price to sub / flag Ray.
checklists.title: Small / Medium Ground Brush
checklists.pricing_guardrail: quote by area / crew-day (~$600–900/crew-day basis) + any rental + disposal. Flat per job.

items.text: IN: small single-story sheds/outbuildings (≈ ≤10×12), wood/metal, hand-demo + haul.

OUT → refer/sub: anything with live electrical or plumbing still connected, structures on a slab needing breaking, anything requiring permits or asbestos/lead handling (older sheds/siding can contain it), multi-story, or attached to the house. If in doubt about age/materials → stop and flag Ray.
Confirm utilities disconnected (power/water) — do NOT demo a shed with live service; flag to Ray to arrange disconnect
Check age/materials — pre-1990 or suspect siding/roofing → asbestos/lead risk → stop, refer for testing
Confirm the slab/foundation stays (we don't break concrete) or it's a refer
Locate property lines, septic, irrigation, buried utility (call 811 if any digging)
Permit check: small accessory-structure demo is usually fine, but if the customer/locale needs a permit, that's a Ray/owner call before we start
PPE: gloves, eye protection, hard hat, sturdy boots, dust mask (demo dust)
De-construct top-down: roof → walls → frame → floor; pull nails/screws, watch for hidden hazards
Sort: clean wood vs. mixed C&D vs. metal (metal may be resale/scrap)
Load + haul; C&D debris pays tonnage (~$73.16/ton) — price it in (this is NOT free veg)
Rake the pad/area clean; before/after photos

guards: Live utilities, slab-breaking, asbestos/lead suspicion, permits, or anything bigger than the cap → refer or escalate to Ray before touching it.
Over a crew-day or needs heavy equipment → price to sub.
checklists.title: Small Shed Demo
checklists.pricing_guardrail: quote by structure size + haul/disposal + access. Flat per job.

items.text: IN: 1- and 2-story gutters reachable from the 30-ft ladder or a water-fed pole.
OUT → refer: 3-story, steep/unsafe roof pitch, or anything past safe ladder reach. No working off the roof edge on a sketchy pitch.

sections.name: Ladder safety (non-negotiable — this is why it's a 2-person job)

items.text: Ladder on firm, level ground; stabilizer/standoff on so it rests off the gutter, not crushing it
Second crew member foots and holds the ladder the entire time someone is on it
3-point contact; never overreach — get down and move the ladder instead
Stay clear of power lines / service drops at the roofline
Wet/windy → reschedule; don't push it
Lay tarps under work zones to catch debris (protect plantings/hardscape)
Scoop debris by hand/trowel into a bucket; bag it
Flush each run with the hose toward the downspout; confirm water flows through
Clear/confirm downspouts (snake or flush blockages); check splash blocks/extensions
Quick look for gutter damage, loose hangers, leaks → note for Ray (don't repair, that's quote-separate)
Rake up fallen debris; haul (clean veg = free disposal)
Before/after photos
Linear feet + stories + roof pitch (safety = the cap)
Access + travel/zone bump
Offer the recurring/seasonal plan + bundle with washing

guards: Past ladder reach / 3-story / unsafe pitch → refer.
Gutter repair, guards install, fascia work = separate quote / possible refer (not a clean-out).
checklists.title: Gutter Cleaning
checklists.pricing_guardrail: by linear footage / stories + access. Flat per job. Bundle with a wash for an easy upsell.
